newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE STOCKS END LOWER, UNDERTONE SEEN FIRM.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE STOCKS END LOWER, UNDERTONE SEEN FIRM.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed lower in volatile trading Thursday but traders expected the market to find its feet early next week.

"Cash flows were too weak to sustain the rise after the market touched a new five-year high," said Miguel Daneri at brokers Boston Securities. "People got scared when they saw the U.S. long bond yield climb above 6.5 percent, which shows that's not a resistance level. But I think this pause won't last beyond Monday."
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.9 percent to 849.88, skidding off a session high of 860.22.
The MerVal, which had closed at a five-year high of 857 Wednesday, trimmed gains in the week to 1.1 percent.

"There's no doubt the bolsa was affected by the poor performance of the U.S. markets today," another trader said. "Prices are struggling higher these days, but because valuations are high, it seems each upward thrust is followed by a moderate correction."
Floor volume fizzled again to 31 million pesos from Wednesday's strong tally of 42.8 million, while over-the-counter turnover slowed to 103.9 million pesos from 129.1 million Wednesday.
The broad market index shed 0.6 percent, with losers outpacing winners 31 to 21 and 23 issues closing flat.

Heaviest main-tier losers were steelmaker Siderca, which fell 2.9 percent, and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, foods giant Molinos Rio de la Plata and holding company Comercial del Plata, all off 2.2 percent.
MerVal gainers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, cement stock Juan Minetti and carmaker Ciadea, which tacked on 4.9 percent, 1.9 percent and 1.6 percent, respectively.
